summary: Block. npm test passes 122 of 122, npm run check passes 11 of 11, and tests/bash-prose.test.mjs passes 15 of 15. Every bypass named from a1 through a4-r2 is now denied: the CR terminator, the xargs heredoc push and the open-construct push. C-2 through C-5 are met. The loop keeps repeating one pattern. The cheaper critic passed twice (a4-r1, a4-r2) without testing how the shell itself reads the text. The strong reviewer then found a place where the guard and the shell disagree about where a heredoc ends, and the builder patched only that one spelling. This round finds the next such disagreement, in the delimiter. dropFileHeredocs line 84 builds the delimiter by deleting every quote and backslash (`word.replace(/["'\\]/g, "")`). The shell instead removes quotes: a backslash inside single quotes stays, and a quote character inside the other kind of quotes stays. So `<<'E\OF'`, `<<"E'OF"`, `<<'E"OF'`, `<<"E\\OF"`, `<<\'EOF` and `<<E\\OF` all end the heredoc for the shell at a body line the guard keeps reading as body. The guard drops the next line, so a reset, a force push to main, a secrets read or rm -rf / that follows is allowed. HEAD denied each of these. I confirmed with echo stand-ins that both real /bin/bash 3.2.57 and /bin/zsh 5.9 run that line, whether the text is run as a file or through eval. This breaks C-1, which drops only the body. It is the a3 F-2 class (partly quoted delimiter) again: the fix handled `E'OF'` and `"E"OF` but not a quote or backslash that sits inside quotes. The earlier findings were correct and none is disputed. The a4-r2 reviewer's notes (a hook or startup-file target, and the pre-existing global-option gaps) still stand. To stop the loop, the fix should accept only delimiters whose quote removal is trivially exact and keep the text whole for any other delimiter. Another hand-written emulation of quote removal would just give the next round a new spelling to find. The criteria are sound and no human hold is needed.

findings.issue: dropFileHeredocs builds the delimiter by deleting every quote and backslash, so the guard reads a delimiter the shell reads with a quote or backslash inside it (`<<'E\OF'`, `<<"E'OF"`, `<<'E"OF'`, `<<"E\\OF"`, `<<\'EOF`, `<<E\\OF`) as `EOF`; the shell ends the heredoc at an earlier body line, and the guard then drops the next command line as body, allowing a reset, force push to main, secrets read or rm -rf / that HEAD denied and that bash and zsh both run.
findings.suggestion: Fail safe on the delimiter instead of emulating quote removal: accept the word only when it is a sequence of plain parts, each one `[\w.-]+`, `'[\w.-]*'`, `"[\w.-]*"` or `\\[\w.-]`. For such a word, deleting the quotes is exact. Otherwise return the text whole. Add D1 through D7 from /tmp/s1-critic-r3/probe.mjs to tests/bash-prose.test.mjs as denied cases. The existing `<<E'OF'` and `<<\\EOF` allow cases still pass under this rule.

findings.issue: GLOBAL_OPTIONS takes `-c\s+\S+`, so a quoted -c value with a space or newline (`git -c "core.x=a b" push origin main`, or the value closed on the next line) leaves a stray quote between git and push, and neither the deny pattern nor the push rule sees the push; HEAD allows it too.
findings.suggestion: A separate goal, together with the a4-r2 reviewer's F-4: treat any quote between `git` and the subcommand as unknown and deny the push.
